content.value_statement: Complex domains can produce unclear boundaries and inconsistent architecture decisions. This skill guides DDD viability, artifact planning, and routing into strategic, tactical, and evented design work.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether full DDD is justified for a business problem.
Defines strategic artifacts such as subdomains, bounded contexts, and glossary terms.
Routes work to specialized DDD, CQRS, event sourcing, saga, projection, and ADR skills.
Requires outputs with scope, assumptions, stage, artifacts, risks, and next steps.
Provides a deliverables checklist for strategic, tactical, and evented design planning.
limitations: Does not replace workshops with domain experts.
Does not generate framework-specific production code.
Not suited for simple CRUD systems with low business complexity.
Requires enough domain context to define terms, boundaries, and invariants.

use_cases.title: Assess DDD Fit
use_cases.description: An engineering lead evaluates whether a billing platform needs full DDD before investing in modeling work.

use_cases.title: Plan Bounded Contexts
use_cases.description: A product architect maps subdomains, ownership, and shared language for teams working on complex workflows.

use_cases.title: Connect Design To Events
use_cases.description: A backend team decides when CQRS, event sourcing, sagas, or projections are justified by domain needs.

prompt_templates.title: Check Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use domain-driven-design to assess whether my application needs DDD. Include assumptions, qualifying signals, risks, and a next step.

prompt_templates.title: Map Strategic Artifacts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use domain-driven-design to define subdomains, bounded contexts, and a glossary for this domain description: [describe domain].

prompt_templates.title: Route Implementation Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use domain-driven-design to route this feature into tactical modeling, CQRS, event sourcing, saga, projection, or ADR work.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Evented Architecture Adoption
prompt_templates.prompt: Use domain-driven-design to evaluate an evented architecture plan. Identify required artifacts, invariants, integration risks, and staged delivery recommendations.

output_examples.input: Assess a subscription billing platform with multiple pricing rules and audit needs.
output: DDD is likely justified because pricing rules, auditability, and team boundaries are significant.
Produce a subdomain map, bounded context map, glossary, and ADR for billing boundaries.
Next route: strategic design, then tactical patterns for aggregates and invariants.

output_examples.input: Plan order fulfillment with warehouse, payment, and shipping teams.
output: The skill separates order, payment, shipping, and inventory contexts.
It identifies translation points and contract risks between teams.
It recommends ADRs before applying CQRS or sagas.

output_examples.input: Decide if a simple admin CRUD tool needs DDD.
output: Full DDD is not recommended because business complexity is low.
Use simpler modular design and document only critical terms.
Revisit DDD if rules or team boundaries become unstable.

best_practices: Start with a viability check before creating DDD artifacts.
Use domain expert language when naming contexts, events, and invariants.
Document boundary decisions in ADRs before selecting implementation patterns.
anti_patterns: Applying full DDD to simple CRUD systems.
Choosing CQRS or event sourcing before proving domain need.
Defining bounded contexts without domain expert input.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It plans architecture artifacts and routes work to specialized implementation skills.

faq.question: Can it replace event storming workshops?
faq.answer: No. It can prepare artifacts, but direct domain expert collaboration is still required.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when business rules, team boundaries, integration contracts, or audit requirements create meaningful complexity.

faq.question: Which tools support it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it support CQRS and event sourcing?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps decide when CQRS, event sourcing, sagas, and projections are appropriate.

faq.question: Is it safe for simple projects?
faq.answer: It is safe to consult, but the skill advises against full DDD for simple low-complexity systems.
